# @jpisgeek/caddy

Manage and retire one explicitly owned route in an existing Linux systemd Caddy
wildcard site through an existing Swamp SSH model. Validate candidates, refuse
drift, verify backend TLS, privately back up changes and roll back failed
reloads without replacing unrelated routes or restarting the service.

**Version** `2026.10.15.1` · **License** MIT · **Source**
https://github.com/jpisgeek/slog-bog/tree/caddy-2026.10.15.1/caddy

## Install

```
swamp extension pull @jpisgeek/caddy
```

## `@jpisgeek/caddy`

### Arguments

| argument     | type   | required | default                         | description                                                             |
| ------------ | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sshModel`   | string | yes      |                                 | Existing @swamp/ssh model; its own credentials remain authoritative     |
| `host`       | string | yes      |                                 | One exact host name in the SSH model                                    |
| `helperPath` | string | no       | `"/usr/local/sbin/swamp-caddy"` | Root-owned helper on the host; the only command the sudoers rule allows |

### Methods

#### `helper`

Emit the helper's exact bytes and digest so an operator can install it
root-owned on the host; nothing runs remotely

No arguments.

#### `inspect`

Read the Caddyfile digest and active service state

No arguments.

#### `plan`

Render and validate one wildcard-host route without replacing live configuration

| argument         | type                      | required | default   | description                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ------------------------- | -------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`           | string                    | yes      |           |                                                                             |
| `hostname`       | string                    | yes      |           |                                                                             |
| `wildcardDomain` | string                    | yes      |           |                                                                             |
| `expectedSha256` | string                    | yes      |           | Digest returned by inspect; refuses changes on drift                        |
| `upstream`       | string                    | yes      |           |                                                                             |
| `upstreamScheme` | `http` \| `https`         | no       | `"https"` | Verified HTTPS by default; cleartext HTTP requires explicit operator opt-in |
| `upstreamCaFile` | string                    | no       |           | Verified public CA PEM on the proxy; required for HTTPS backends            |
| `allowedCidrs`   | array of string \| string | yes      |           |                                                                             |

#### `apply`

Validate, privately back up, atomically replace and reload one route; roll back
on reload failure

| argument         | type                      | required | default   | description                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ------------------------- | -------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`           | string                    | yes      |           |                                                                             |
| `hostname`       | string                    | yes      |           |                                                                             |
| `wildcardDomain` | string                    | yes      |           |                                                                             |
| `expectedSha256` | string                    | yes      |           | Digest returned by inspect; refuses changes on drift                        |
| `upstream`       | string                    | yes      |           |                                                                             |
| `upstreamScheme` | `http` \| `https`         | no       | `"https"` | Verified HTTPS by default; cleartext HTTP requires explicit operator opt-in |
| `upstreamCaFile` | string                    | no       |           | Verified public CA PEM on the proxy; required for HTTPS backends            |
| `allowedCidrs`   | array of string \| string | yes      |           |                                                                             |

#### `remove`

Remove one exact managed route after a digest check, private backup and full
validation; preserve every other route

| argument         | type   | required | default | description                                          |
| ---------------- | ------ | -------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`           | string | yes      |         |                                                      |
| `hostname`       | string | yes      |         |                                                      |
| `wildcardDomain` | string | yes      |         |                                                      |
| `expectedSha256` | string | yes      |         | Digest returned by inspect; refuses changes on drift |

### Data written

| resource       | lifetime | fields                                                                                                                            | description                                                                    |
| -------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `operation`    | 7d       | `requestId`, `action`, `beforeSha256`, `afterSha256`, `changed`, `validated`, `serviceActive`, `backupPath`, `route`, `transport` | Correlated Caddy operation; no full configuration or credentials               |
| `helperDigest` | 7d       | `sha256`, `bytes`                                                                                                                 | Digest and size of emitted helper bytes; not an inspection of a remote service |

## Example

```yaml
# Stored model globals; YOUR_* are placeholders, not deployment names.
globalArguments:
  sshModel: YOUR_SSH_MODEL
  host: YOUR_HOST
  helperPath: /usr/local/sbin/swamp-caddy

---
# plan/apply method arguments: use inspect's current beforeSha256.
# The trusted operator supplies a public CA PEM on the proxy first.
name: notes
hostname: notes.example.com
wildcardDomain: example.com
upstream: backend.example.com:8443
upstreamScheme: https
upstreamCaFile: /etc/caddy/trust/example-root-ca.pem
allowedCidrs: ["192.0.2.0/24"]
expectedSha256: REPLACE_WITH_INSPECTED_SHA256
```

## Caveats

**Compatibility:** tested with Swamp `20261014.121640.0-sha.c5d1db96` (native
`ctx.runModel` resource handles and definition UUID lookup),
`@swamp/ssh@2026.10.13.1`, Python 3.9+ and Caddy 2.11.7. The declared platforms
describe the Swamp controller, not a macOS systemd target. The target is Linux
with an already active `caddy` service. This extension does not bootstrap the
service, DNS or backend. Validation provisions real Caddy modules and can create
module state, including local PKI keys and CAs; only use configuration and
modules reviewed by the privileged operator.

**Install deliberately:** call `helper` to emit the pinned helper and its digest
(this does not inspect the target). An authorized operator must install those
exact bytes at `helperPath`, root-owned mode 0755, under root-owned
non-group/world-writable parents. The narrowly scoped sudoers command is
`/usr/local/sbin/swamp-caddy`, never a shell or Python interpreter. Protect
model configuration and any allowed custom helperPath as privileged operator
input. Upgrades fail closed until the new helper is installed.

The helper fixes `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`, `/usr/bin/caddy`, and
`/usr/bin/systemctl`; these paths cannot be overridden. Protected paths must not
contain symlinks or writable/untrusted ancestors. Optional
`/etc/caddy/caddy.env` supplies simple KEY=VALUE defaults; this is not a general
systemd EnvironmentFile parser. Ensure its effective validation environment
matches the running service before use.

Run `inspect`, `plan`, then `apply` serially in a Swamp workflow, binding each
method to the successful inspection's digest. A plan provisions real Caddy
modules in a private staged directory. All methods, including inspect,
create/use the persistent empty root-owned `/etc/caddy/.swamp-caddy.lock`. It
does not replace or reload the live configuration, but is not literally
filesystem-read-only. A stale digest refuses the operation. An unchanged apply
still reloads to reconcile an interrupted previous operation. Validation does
not probe backend reachability; backend certificate and hostname verification
happen when Caddy forwards a request.

**Concurrency precondition:** every writer of the Caddyfile, including
administrators and other automation, must hold an exclusive flock on that same
lock file across its edit and reload. Do not use this helper alongside writers
that ignore the lock. The helper serializes its own invocations and checks
bytes, inode, ownership, permissions and timestamps for observed drift; these
checks are not filesystem compare-and-swap against an uncooperative root writer.
Atomic replacement alone cannot provide that guarantee.

Exactly one plain `*.example.com {` header is supported for a selected wildcard
domain. Imports, CRLF, ambiguous/noncanonical owned blocks and unmanaged
occurrences of the desired hostname are refused. Matching existing hostnames is
case-insensitive and ignores a terminal dot. Removal requires only name,
hostname, wildcardDomain and expectedSha256; it removes a complete canonical
block with that exact identity, validates and reloads. Absent removal is
idempotent. Always inspect after errors.

**Migration:** old configurable binary/config globals were removed. HTTPS now
defaults on: supply a public CA PEM under `/etc/caddy/trust/` (root-owned,
protected parents, at most 64 KiB, no private key). Explicit
`upstreamScheme: http` opts into cleartext and forbids a CA field. HTTP exposes
forwarded headers, cookies, authorization and request/response bodies to the
backend network; use it only on a separately protected hop. Normal
certificate/hostname verification stays on; there is no insecure TLS switch.
Canonical non-universal client CIDRs are mandatory, and their union must not
cover all IPv4 or all IPv6 clients.

Tests include disposable transaction success/failure/rollback/retirement
fixtures and native child-evidence admission tests. The separate Linux CI
integration exercises real Caddy and systemd with disposable localhost TLS
resources; it requires an empty hosted runner and refuses preexisting Caddy
resources. It is never a production proxy check or a grant to deploy there.

## Security

Root helper privilege is a real operator capability. Native child calls use the
existing `@swamp/ssh` definition, not a new credential or nested CLI. They are
delegated model capability, **not** a per-target grant check for the triggering
principal. Allow only fixed reviewed workflows/configuration; do not expose
arbitrary method inputs as an unrestricted public run surface. The SSH model
remains responsible for connection/host-key policy.

Success requires one current-invocation resource with matching definition, host,
method, name and request/action identifiers; latest-result fallback is
forbidden. Unknown execution inputs and contradictory helper answers fail
without writing an operation observation. Schema validation is not a general
secret detector and cannot make an untrusted SSH server honest.

Full Caddyfiles remain on the proxy. Subprocess stderr is discarded, not
preserved for later diagnosis, because it can expose credentials. The helper
bounds stdout and deadlines, uses the cooperative exclusive lock, validates
before replacing, and restores/reloads the original on reload failure unless
observed content or metadata drift makes rollback unsafe. Cancellation does not
guarantee an elevated operation stopped or undo an already committed change.
Failed/ambiguous runs require a fresh inspection; they are never recorded as
successful observations.

Remote full-configuration backups are private (directory 0700/files 0600),
capped at five recognized owned regular files even after failed reloads. They
can include unrelated inline secrets from the original configuration; prefer
protected external secret references. There is no backup age limit: operators
must delete unwanted backups deliberately. Normal exits remove private staging
directories; crashes/power loss can leave private staged copies requiring
inspected operator cleanup. Neither is public output. Foreign files and symlinks
are never pruned. Operation observations contain selected route
host/upstream/CIDRs/CA path, digests, status, backup path and an exact
child-evidence pointer; these can still be operationally sensitive. `inspect`,
`plan`, `apply` and `remove` are per-model versioned result streams, not
per-route inventory. Bind the current run's exact resource version and
requestId, not a later latest-result lookup. Keeping these names stable also
bounds version-stream cardinality instead of creating a stream per request. They
declare a 7-day/20-version policy; helper files/digests declare 7-day/5-version
policies. Actual deletion requires Swamp GC configuration and execution; expiry
is not guaranteed immediate physical deletion.

The dependency `@swamp/ssh` is separately licensed (AGPL); this extension's MIT
license does not relicense it. Its script runner records connection metadata,
interpreter/sudo/script byte count and potentially sensitive stdout/stderr, not
the full supplied script. Its runResult has infinite lifetime and its model
runHistory/GC settings govern version retention (default 50), not this
extension's policies. Protect those records and review that configuration. The
community `@evrardjp/caddy` was a design reference; no source was copied.

See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/jpisgeek/slog-bog/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
for the release gates every version passes before it reaches the registry.
